story.fullStory:
Asia's "Heat Of The Moment" reached #4 on the Billboard Hot 100. "Heat of the Moment" is the first single released by English progressive rock supergroup Asia from their 1982 eponymous debut album.

It was written by singer and bass guitarist John Wetton and keyboardist Geoff Downes.

It was named by Lee Zimmerman of Paste as Asia's signature song.

The song peaked at #4 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 18 weeks on the chart.

evidence.recording:
4 recording notes captured

It was written by singer and bass guitarist John Wetton and keyboardist Geoff Downes.

No-one else particularly "got" the song, and it was the last song to be recorded for the album.

After the release of Karma, Fulber left to pursue other interests, and Leeb teamed up with producer Chris Peterson to release Poem.

In 2000, three years after Karma was released, notable DJs such as Tiësto and Airscape produced remixes of "Silence", which generated interest and gained considerable radio airplay for the original track, albeit most airplay was for the remixes.
